facts: **Interpolation** predicts a value that lies within the range of the recorded data.
**Extrapolation** predicts a value outside the recorded data — below the smallest recorded value, or beyond the largest.
Read the predicted value from the line of best fit, not from the nearest plotted point.
Interpolation is generally reliable because it is supported by recorded data on both sides.
Extrapolation is less reliable, because nothing shows the relationship continues unchanged beyond the recorded range.
The further a prediction lies beyond the recorded data, the less reliable it becomes.
steps: Decide whether the value to be predicted lies inside the recorded range (interpolation) or outside it (extrapolation)
Read the corresponding value from the line of best fit
State the prediction, noting that an extrapolated prediction is less reliable

workedExamples.question_text:
A nursery measured seedlings from week $2$ to week $10$. A straight line fitted the heights closely over those weeks. A student claims that the same line will predict their heights at week $156$ just as reliably.

Is this claim reasonable? Explain using the recorded range and the likely growth pattern.
workedExamples.solution_text:
No. Week $156$ is far outside the recorded range of $2$ to $10$ weeks, so this is extreme extrapolation.

A close fit during the recorded weeks does not show that the same growth rate continues for three years. Growth may slow as the plants mature, making the long-term linear prediction unreliable.

mastery.solution_text:
Week $5$ lies within the recorded range (week $3$ to week $6$), so predicting the height at week $5$ is interpolation. The line gives $20$ cm.
Week $10$ lies well beyond the recorded range, so predicting the height at week $10$ is extrapolation. The line gives $35$ cm.
The week $5$ prediction is more trustworthy, because it is interpolation, supported by recorded data on both sides.

mastery.question_text: A student says, "Since my line of best fit is very accurate for the recorded weeks, I can extrapolate it to predict the plant's height in $5$ years' time with the same accuracy." Explain why the student is incorrect.
mastery.solution_text:
A line of best fit is only shown to be accurate within the range it was fitted to, using the recorded data.
Extrapolating $5$ years beyond a few recorded weeks assumes the same linear growth rate continues indefinitely, but plants mature, slow their growth, or stop growing entirely.
How well the line fits the recorded weeks says nothing about how well it predicts far outside that range.
